description.narrative: The Program Development Objective is to increase the volume of added-value products commercialized in selected agri-food value chains in the Program area.

The development objective of the Strengthening Agri-Food Value-Chains Program-for-Results Project for Morocco is to increase the volume of added-value products commercialized in selected agri-food value chains in the Program area. The proposed operation would contribute to the World Bank Group's twin goals of eliminating extreme poverty and boosting shared prosperity in a sustainable manner. It will improve the integration of Morocco's small and medium agri-food producers and enterprises in agri-food value chains, as well as strengthen the resilience and sustainability of the selected value chains. The proposed operation is aligned with the Country Partnership Strategy (CPS) 2014-2017. the program would support the three strategic result areas of the CPS : (1) promoting competitive and inclusive growth; (2) building a green and resilient future; and (3) strengthening governance and institutions for improved services. The Program's support for increased investment in agri-food processing and aggregation, innovative products and green technologies and practices, as well as improved food safety and quality would contribute to increase the productivity and value-added of the agri-food sector. The Program's support for improved sector planning and budgeting processes as well as integrated program monitoring, evaluation and reporting systems would contribute to the achievement of enable more transparent and accountable management of public resources through budget and procurement reforms. The proposed operation contributes to the implementation of the World Bank Group's MENA regional strategy's pillar on renewal of the social contract, with an emphasis on more inclusive economic growth.

title.narrative: Interprofessions with business plans approved and intra-branch agreements adopted to ensure sust.

comment.narrative: The Program indicator was achieved in December 2021. The interprofessions Interprolive/Maroc Citrus were instrumental in supporting producers to commercialize citrus/olives/high-quality olive oil including through capacity-building and advisory (e.g., related to export requirements and related marketing, agronomic practices, conditioning etc.).

title.narrative: Area treated for Mediterranean fruit fly through the new Center

comment.narrative: The Program failed to achieve the indicator target as the center for the production of sterilized ceratitis was operationalized only in September 2024. Until completion, the Program repeatedly imported sterilized ceratitis flies from Spain to treat a more limited area (5800 ha). The center is currently in the process of ramping up capacity.

title.narrative: Interprofessions with business plans approved and intra-branch agreements adopted to ensure sust.

comment.narrative: The two milestones to strengthen the Interprofessions (approval of a business plan by the management of the in terprofession and by MAPMDREF, and adoption of an Accord Interprofessionnel by members of the interprofession through its General Assembly) have been completed for Maroc-Citrus and Interprolive.

title.narrative: Small- and/or medium-size producers and/or enterprises assisted by the Agri-food Innovation Center

comment.narrative:
Small- and/or medium-size producers and enterprises with value-addition projects that have requested and benefitted from at least one of the services offered by the Agri-Food Innovation Centers (CIA). Services include technical support services; management support services; knowledge and market access support services; incubation support services, and networking services).
The CIA in MeknEs (CENAM) provided pesticide testing services to 5 citrus producers and 1 olive producer, facilitating market access and commercialization/export.
The Program failed to achieve its target due to the late operationalization of the CIA in Berkane (September 2024).

comment.narrative: Small- and/or medium-size producers and enterprises with value-addition projects that have requested and benefitted from at least one of the services offered by the CIAs (technical support services; management support services; knowledge and market access support services; incubation support services, and networking services). This indicator will be disaggregated by gender (owner in case of enterprises)

comment.narrative: The indicator aggregates all projects adopting green practices and technologies, including those to treat olive crushing residues and enhance climate adaptation and mitigation, either as a result of the support provided by the CIAs or within the scope of FDA's financial support.

title.narrative: Producers with an input register in the Souss-Massa region

comment.narrative: This Program exceeded its target related to the number of agricultural producers who are using an input register in the Souss-Massa region (achievement rate 194%). The adoption of the register by 1566 citrus producers strengthened their capacity to meet export requirements related to phytosanitary standards and, therefore, supported progress towards the PDO.

title.narrative: Private investments in conditioning, cold storage and/or processing units (olive, citrus) generated

comment.narrative:
It should be noted that this indicator has not been correctly reflected by the operations portal. As per the PAD, the unit of this indicator is "Value in MDM (Million Dirham)" and the target value should be "700".
The indicator captures the value of private investment in conditioning, cold storage and/or processing units for projects receiving incentives from the FDA (olive, citrus) under adjusted modalities for appraisal and monitoring by MAPMDREF. The Program mobilized a total of DHM 2.6 bn in private capital until closure, exceeding the target by more than 300%.

title.narrative: Private investments in conditioning, cold storage and/or processing units (olive, citrus) generated

comment.narrative: More than 132 units achieved under this activity.
Number of additional producers aggregated within the scope of the Program, disaggregated by gender

The Program did not achieve the target (achievement 59%) due to (i) the delay in implementation of the amended law 04-12 and (ii) the impacts of prolonged drought.
However, under the government's Green Generation Strategy 2020-2030 (the current sectoral strategy following the PMV), additional aggregation projects for olive (28 projects) and citrus producers (20 projects) have been identified.

title.narrative: Volume of high quality olive oil commercialized (i.e. quality is higher than lampante)

comment.narrative:
Annual indicator. Contrary to the initially planned data collection methodology consisting of annual surveys, values related to this PDO indicator were mainly estimated through an alternative statistical approach agreed between the PMU and the World Bank agreed in June 2022 (with the exception of 2018/2019 when a survey was conducted). In 2022/2023 MAPMDREF conducted a survey, which, however, proved unrepresentative due to drought impacts.
The values recorded in results framework after ISMs frequently differed from final values reported in annual progress reports, including due to methodological challenges and mismatch between ISM timing and data collection cycles (see also explanation under PDO#1 and PDO#2).
The Program did not achieve the target due to low olive oil production in the 2022/2023 and the 2023/2024 agricultural seasons. However, according to annual progress reports, the final indicator values for 2019 and 2022 reached 18,660 t and 16,100 t, respectively.

title.narrative: Volume of high quality olive oil commercialized (i.e. quality is higher than lampante)

comment.narrative: The final value for 2022 reached 80,5% of the target (16,000) . Although the target of 20,000 tonnes of high quality olive oil, was not reached, the indicator showed good progress during the program period; the average volume during the program implementation period was around 1,170 tonnes, i.e. 32% up on the estimated baseline of 10,000 tonnes. Excluding years of severe drought ,which coincide with the final phase of the program, the evolution of ODP indicator n°3 shows an increase of around 45% compared to the reference.

title.narrative: Use of market information services for mobile phones and of the application Publi-Asaar

comment.narrative: This indicator aggregates the following: (i) additional SMS sent to users (160,000 at EOP), and (ii) additional downloads of the mobile application (40,000 at EOP).

title.narrative: Small and/or medium enterprises agri-food authorized by ONSSA

comment.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of additional SME in the agri-food sector authorized by ONSSA, reflecting their compliance with food safety regulations. The indicator target was exceeded substantially (The total number of ONSSA-authorized SME reached 1103 of which 1000 were verified through the IGA under DLI#5).

title.narrative: Small and/or medium enterprises agri-food authorized by ONSSA

comment.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of additional small and/or medium enterprises (as defined by Maroc PME), authorized by ONSSA, reflecting their compliance with the food safety law. This indicator will be disaggregated by gender (owner in case of enterprises)

title.narrative: Volume of conditioned and exported citrus

comment.narrative: Volume of conditioned and exported citrus. This is an annual indicator that depends heavily on the availability of irrigation water. For December 2022, the final value achieved is : 765,684 T , which is higher than the target of the program (750,000 T).

title.narrative: Volume of conditioned and exported citrus

comment.narrative:
Annual indicator. Indicator measures total citrus exports during the citrus agricultural campaign, which runs from 1 September year n to 31 August of year n+1.
As the timing ISMs was not aligned with the data collection cycle, indicator values recorded in results framework after ISMs frequently differed slightly from final values reported in annual progress reports (see annex 6 for overview of final indicator values).
The indicator depends heavily on the availability of irrigation water. With the support of the Program's interventions, the indicator exceeded its target during the 2021/2022 season, reaching 765,661 t. However, due to unprecedented drought and the ensuing irrigation water shortages, primary production declined significantly. As a result, indicator values dropped below their baseline in the season 2022/2023 until Program closure.

title.narrative: Volume of conditioned and exported olives

comment.narrative: This is an annual indicator that depends heavily on rainfall and the availability of irrigation water. For December 2022, the final value achieved is 100,937 T, which is higher than the target of the program (98,000 T).

title.narrative: Volume of conditioned and exported olives

comment.narrative:
Annual indicator. Annual values measure total volume of table olive exports from 1 January to 31 December of a given year. Final value for 2024 corresponds to total exports registered from January - September 2024.
As the timing ISMs were not aligned with the data collection cycle, indicator values recorded in results framework after ISMs frequently differed from final values reported in annual progress reports (see annex 6 for overview of final indicator values).
The indicator depends heavily on the availability of rainfall and irrigation water. During the 2020/2021 and 2021/2022 seasons, the indicator surpassed the Program targets. However, due to unprecedented drought and the ensuing irrigation water shortages, primary production declined significantly. As a result, indicator values fell significantly starting 2023 with the final indicator value below its baseline in September 2024.
